product.name: Patchlane
product.descriptor: Configuration checks for small development teams
product.headline: Catch missing configuration before release.
product.intro: Define the environment keys your project expects, then run a repeatable check from your terminal or CI job. Patchlane reports missing names without printing secret values.
product.contactNote: Fictional contact address; this page does not send messages or schedule demos.

features.title: One expected-key list
features.body: Keep required and optional environment key names in a small project file that can be reviewed with your code.

features.title: Readable local results
features.body: See which key names are present, missing or optional. Values stay out of the report.

features.title: CI-friendly exit status
features.body: Use the same check in a pipeline. A missing required key produces a failing status so the team can investigate.

features.title: Profiles for each environment
features.body: Define separate expected-key lists for development, staging and production without copying secret values into the configuration file.

features.title: Share a check summary
features.body: Export a plain-text summary of key names and check results to include with a release note.

features.title: Team conventions
features.body: Paid plans add shared check templates and workspace roles for teams that want a common starting point.

workflow.title: List expected keys
workflow.body: Add the required and optional names to patchlane.json. Keep secret values in your existing environment setup.

workflow.title: Run a check
workflow.body: Use the local command while preparing a change, or run it as a CI step.

workflow.title: Review missing names
workflow.body: Read the report, update your environment and check again before releasing.

faq.question: Is Patchlane a secret manager?
faq.answer: No. In this fictional product brief, it checks whether expected key names are set. It does not store secrets, rotate credentials or replace your existing secret manager.

faq.question: Does a passing check prove my configuration is correct?
faq.answer: No. It confirms that the expected names have values. It does not prove that a token is valid, a service is reachable or the application will work.

faq.question: Can I use the same check in CI?
faq.answer: Yes, as described by the supplied product concept. A missing required key returns a failing exit status. The output shown on this page is only an example.

faq.question: Do I need a paid plan for local checks?
faq.answer: No. Local includes local and CI checks. Paid plans add shared workspaces and team features.

faq.question: Is annual billing available?
faq.answer: No annual option is included in this example. The paid prices shown are monthly USD prices.

faq.question: Can I buy or install it from this page?
faq.answer: No. Patchlane is fictional. Plan buttons show local previews and the copy button only copies the example command. There is no checkout, account creation or package execution.
